articles.summary: A rejection never reached adjudication. A denial did. The two words get used interchangeably, and the confusion costs providers real money. A rejection and a denial are not the same. They do not have the same cause, the same fix, or the same clock. Teams that treat them as one bucket lose money in ways that are hard to see on a report.
articles.title: Rejection vs. denial, and why the difference costs you money

articles.summary: Financial clearance, clean claims, denials, reconciliation. A plain map of what the revenue cycle is actually trying to get done, and which job hurts most.
articles.title: The four jobs of revenue cycle, and why denials is the hardest

articles.summary: Abandoning a small denial was never laziness. It was arithmetic. Here is the arithmetic, the sourced cost of reworking a claim, and what changes when the cost falls.
articles.title: Small dollar denials: why RCM teams abandon them, and why that math just changed
